Many IELTS aspirants are finding IELTS reading module as the most challenging part in IELTS exam. Here are few reasons for this. The major challenge is that the IELTS reading module will require immense concentration. For IELTS reading, in just 60 minutes, you need to read three long passages and have to answer 40 questions. Thus, reading the questions properly, understanding them and answering them properly are a challenging task with the ticking clock. Here Casper Academy of Excellence, the best IELTS training institute in Ernakulam is giving you few tips to improve your IELTS reading score.

Difficulty Level of Passages

Another reason for the difficulty of IELTS reading is the difficulty level of the passages. For IELTS Academic reading, the passages might be narrative, descriptive or argumentative. Moreover, it may contain diagrams or graphs. Due to this the passages might be lengthy. For IELTS general reading, passages are usually taken from advertisements, books, magazines, notices and more. Thus, it will become a difficult task with comprehending passages with different levels of difficulty and answering them.

What makes IELTS Reading Test Tough?

The four major points that will make IELTS reading difficult are:

  • You may run short of time.
  • You will be under pressure to answer each question correctly within the given time.
  • Unable to attempt few questions, because you don’t have time.
  • You may get confused with different words with similar meaning used by the examiner.

All these reasons will definitely make the IELTS reading module tough for the aspirants. Casper Academy of Excellence is giving solutions to cope with these problems. With best coaching and teaching modules, Casper Academy is the best IELTS coaching centre in Kochi.

What are Keywords in IELTS Reading?

Keywords are the words that will carry some specific information. Due to this, the importance of IELTS Reading will always exist in this module. These words will be useful in making the reader to identify the context of the passage.  So that, in return, it will help the test taker to find correct answer.

Which words can be your Keywords?

Those things that can be included as your keywords are as follows:

  • Names (places, people and more in the passage)
  • Nouns and verbs
  • Locations (countries, states, cities, towns, etc.)
  • Dates and years
  • Numbers or figures
  • Capitalized or italicized words or phrases in the passage.

What are Keyword Synonyms?

Keyword synonyms are those words that are same or are having nearly similar meaning as the keyword. They are also called parallel expressions. For example, Children – Kids, Present – Gift are few words with similar meaning. Knowing about these things will make your IELTS Reading module easier.
